title: 5 total days of work with Claude and Meshy, Blender
author: InvestigatorCalm3640
selftext:
I've been working on a 3D hunt-or-be-hunted wildlife simulation for iPhone and iPad called [prey or pray](https://apps.apple.com/ly/app/prey-or-pray/id6822941090), using Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5), Blender and Meshy. you pick an animal and either survive as prey (graze, drink, watch the wind, outrun whatever's hunting you) or play the predator and actually have to stalk and catch something. there are 6 habitats (rockies, serengeti, kanha in india, himalaya, denali, patagonia) and 57 animals you can play.



I wanted to make the game as realistic as I could get it to be, so the animals run on real numbers from field studies. a cheetah hits 93 km/h but is gassed after about 20 seconds, and wolves win by just wearing things down. there's also a field journal where you log real behaviours when you see them happen, like a gazelle stotting or hyenas stealing a kill.



claude code (fable 5.2 and opus 5.5) wrote basically all of the code: the simulation, the animal AI, the renderer, menus, multiplayer. i mostly played it on my phone and told it when something looked or felt wrong. it even made this video, recording the game in the simulator with the AI playing each animal and editing it with ffmpeg.

comments.author: GaumeoproStudio
comments.body: Honestly, this is pretty incredible for just five days of work. What really stands out to me isn’t just the graphics, but the depth of the simulation and the fact that you’re using real animal behavior and field data. Having the option to experience both sides of the predator-prey relationship makes the concept even more interesting. The field journal is a really nice touch, too. It’s impressive how much you managed to build with AI as part of your workflow. I’m curious, roughly how many tokens did you end up using with Fable and Opus 5.5?
